Definition: third person singular present indicative of G1510; he (she or it) is; also (with neuter plural) they are:--are, be(-long), call, X can(-not), come, consisteth, X dure for a while, + follow, X have, (that) is (to say), make, meaneth, X must needs, + profit, + remaineth, + wrestle.
BiblicalUsage: Estí is the word for 'is' — the third-person singular of the verb to be. It is the commonest little word in the New Testament, the hinge of almost every sentence about who God is and who we are. 'Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven' turns on it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe estí earns its study because so much hangs on it: what a thing is, who a person is, and what God says is true.
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; The Sermon on the Mount
